title: Đốt có kiểm soát để phòng cháy rừng · Advantages / Disadvantages
prompt: Some governments are considering allowing carefully controlled burning to reduce wildfire risks. Do the advantages of this policy outweigh the disadvantages?

source.detail: Bài luyện mở rộng biên soạn riêng cho năm 2026. Tham khảo các nhóm chủ đề trong forecast công khai; tình huống, bài mẫu và phân tích được viết mới.
source.disclaimer: Không xác nhận đề này đã xuất hiện hoặc sẽ xuất hiện trong kỳ thi. Các chủ đề ngách được bổ sung để mở rộng phạm vi luyện tập; không gán xác suất ra thi.

keywords: Đốt có kiểm soát để phòng cháy rừng Khi vật liệu dễ cháy tích nhiều năm, một điểm bắt lửa có thể thành đám cháy mà lực lượng thông thường không thể khống chế an toàn. Rủi ro cháy tương lai thấp hơn không biện hộ hại tức thời có thể tránh, nên phương pháp phòng ngừa phải hợp địa hình và dân cư.
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.
paragraphs: A practical reason for allowing carefully controlled burning to reduce wildfire risks is that removing accumulated vegetation through planned burns can reduce the fuel available to an uncontrolled fire, potentially protecting settlements and sensitive woodland nearby. On balance, I consider the potential advantages greater, provided that the response to the main drawback is built into delivery: permits should depend on weather thresholds, trained personnel and local health safeguards, with mechanical vegetation removal preferred where burning cannot be justified safely.

When combustible material builds up for many years, a single ignition can develop into a fire that ordinary emergency crews cannot safely contain. For example, a forestry team could burn a limited area during suitable weather, with trained crews present and residents warned about temporary smoke exposure. A lower future fire risk does not excuse avoidable immediate harm, so prevention methods must be matched to the landscape and nearby population. Communities need advance notice and clear cancellation rules, so a preventive operation is not allowed to proceed merely because crews and equipment have already been booked.

A planned burn can escape its intended boundary, and repeated smoke exposure may harm people living nearby even when no property is destroyed. This difficulty becomes more serious when burning targets are pursued despite unsuitable wind conditions, or communities with respiratory vulnerabilities have no effective warning or temporary protection. Permits should depend on weather thresholds, trained personnel and local health safeguards, with mechanical vegetation removal preferred where burning cannot be justified safely.
Controlled burning can reduce future wildfire damage, but only trained teams operating within credible weather and health limits should be permitted to undertake it.
